items.title: Dissolution de l’Assemblée nationale : « Il n’y a pas de fixation » selon le Président de la République
items.description: En marge de la 81ᵉ session de l’Assemblée générale des Nations unies à New York, le président de la République, Bassirou Diomaye Faye s’est exprimé dans un entretien exclusif accordé à France 24 et RFI sur plusieurs dossiers majeurs de l’actualité sénégalaise et régionale. Interrogé sur l’éventualité d’une dissolution de l’Assemblée nationale à partir du 2 décembre prochain, date à laquelle cette prérogative constitutionnelle pourrait être exercée, le chef de l’État s’est gardé d’exclure cette éventualité. « Il n’y a pas de fixation » sur l’option d’une dissolution, a-t-il précisé. Le président de la République rappelle ainsi qu’il dispose, en vertu de la Constitution, de cette prérogative et laisse entendre que sa décision dépendra de la configuration qui se présentera à lui. « Selon ce qu’on aura en face, on décidera », a-t-il déclaré. Président en exercice de la CEDEAO, Bassirou Diomaye Faye est également revenu sur ses relations avec les pays membres de la Confédération des États du Sahel (AES), qui ont quitté l’organisation régionale. Le choix du Mali comme première destination de son déplacement dans le cadre de cette responsabilité régionale n’est pas anodin. Le Président affirme toutefois inscrire sa démarche dans une logique de dialogue et de respect de la souveraineté des États concernés. « Mon objectif est de garantir une coexistence entre les deux blocs et la libre circulation des personnes et des biens », a-t-il expliqué. Face à la rupture entre la CEDEAO et les trois pays de l’AES (Mali, Burkina Faso et Niger), Dakar entend ainsi privilégier une approche fondée sur le maintien des liens entre les populations et les économies de la région. « Nous n’avons pas de sens interdit », affirme le chef de l’État. O.BA

items.title: Deputy Minority Leader appeals to First Lady, Vice President over Salomey Baffoe’s detention
items.description: The Deputy Minority Leader in Parliament, Patricia Appiagyei, has appealed to the First Lady, Lordina Mahama and the Vice President, Jane Naana Opoku-Agyemang, to intervene in the case of Salomey Awiti Baffoe, whose bail application was denied by the High Court. Speaking with JoyNews , Madam Appiagyei expressed concern about the continued detention of Ms Baffoe, particularly her responsibilities as a mother, describing it as particularly ‘disturbing’ in a country where many women are single mothers. “It is very unfortunate. We are using women against other women. I would like to make a passionate appeal to our First Lady and our Vice President that what is happening is very disturbing, especially in Ghana, where most of the women are single mothers,” she stated. According to her, Ms Baffoe is responsible for caring for her children and ensuring that they attend school, making the situation especially difficult for the family. “This is a very serious occasion of a woman who is single-handedly taking care of the children and she has to see to it that the child attends school within the day,” she said. Madam Appiagyei urged the two female leaders to ensure that the interests and welfare of women in situations such as Ms Baffoe’s are given due consideration. Her comments follow the High Court’s decision on Thursday, September 24, to refuse bail for Ms Baffoe, who is facing a charge of abetting the publication of false news in the “Ghana Jollof” TikTok case.

Italy bans burqas in schools, caps number of foreign students per class
items.description: Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni’s cabinet adopted a decree law Thursday banning burqas and niqabs in schools and capping the number of students with a poor command of Italian per class. It introduces “A 30 percent cap on the number of students in a class who do not have an adequate command of Italian, more tools for learning our language, and a ban on the burqa and niqab in schools,” Meloni wrote on social media. If a child seriously struggles to integrate at school, social services will be called and the parents will be obliged to attend free Italian lessons. Failure to comply will be punished with a fine of up to 1,000 euros ($1,140). Italy is a frontline country for migration and integration is a hot campaign issue ahead of next year’s general election. Save the Children warned forcing children to change schools or enrol in a different institution from their peers simply because of their nationality or limited proficiency in Italian would “create ‘first-class’ and ‘second-class’ students”. But Education Minister Giuseppe Valditara said “inadequate language proficiency… hinders educational progress”. “Parental participation in their child’s educational path is fundamental for academic success”, he told journalists. Valditara said there were 34,000 school classes in Italy in which over 30 percent of the students are foreign. But most of those would be not be affected by the new law, which targets new arrivals rather than those born in Italy or who attended kindergarten. The 30 percent limit on the number of foreign students per class was established in a ministerial memorandum in 2010. But the limit was flexible, and could be raised in cases involving foreign students with adequate language skills, such as foreign students born in Italy, or lowered when foreign students have a poor command of Italian. Opposition leader Elly Schlein accused the government of “a new witch hunt at the expense of children”. The burqa ban was “a matter of security”, Meloni said in a television interview after the cabinet meeting. “When a woman — or worse, a young girl — is forced to cover her face, she is being denied fundamental rights and the very integration that is so often loudly championed,” she said. A crackdown on the use of burqas in schools was called for in July by the National Future (FN) party. The FN, which is not part of the governing coalition, is further to the right than Meloni’s and has emerged as a major challenger, rising sharply in the polls since launching in February. AFP The post Italy bans burqas in schools, caps number of foreign students per class appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: ‘Never again’, APC cautions Nigerians against voting Atiku in 2027
items.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The All Progressives Congress APC has cautioned Nigerians against voting former Vice President Atiku Abubakar into power in the 2027 presidential election, warning that he must never again be allowed anywhere near the nation’s treasury. National Publicity Secretary of the APC, Felix Morka in a statement on Thursday notes that the media and public discourse had been awash with damning reports of Atiku’s alleged dealings in local and international bribery and corruption schemes. The APC described the remarks as “an open and shut reference by the former President, Atiku’s principal, to his unfitness for public office,” concluding that Atiku “was an accidental Vice President, and categorically unfit for the office of President of the Federal Republic of Nigeria.” “Ghosts of his sordid past continue, restlessly, to haunt and warn that Atiku must never again be allowed anywhere close to such a commanding position of trust and responsibility as the presidency,” the statement read. APC describes Atiku’s record as a former public official as “an executive summary of some of Nigeria’s vilest episodes of corruption and cronyism that pulverized our economy and decimated public trust.” The party said the upcoming presidential election presented the electorate the opportunity to deal a final blow to Atiku’s quest for presidential power, listing a string of controversies it said spanned decades, from “the Mambilla Hydroelectric Power Project and the Siemens bribery scandal to the William Jefferson case, the PTDF funds controversy, and the US Senate investigation into suspicious financial transactions.” The APC insisted these were not mere allegations, stating that they were “matters that are well documented in official records, tribunal proceedings, government investigations, national and foreign legislative reports, and international financial inquiries,” which it said raised legitimate questions about Atiku’s fitness for probity and accountability as a serial presidential contender. On the Mambilla project, the statement said an International Chamber of Commerce Arbitration Tribunal in Paris had examined a $500,000 payment made in January 2003 by Leno Adesanya, promoter of Sunrise Power, to Jennifer Douglas, Atiku’s wife at the time, through an offshore company, a payment it said occurred around the period the Mambilla contract was awarded with Atiku as Vice President, adding that Atiku “declined an opportunity to explain and justify what clearly was an illegal bribe payment to his wife.” The party also recalled the Siemens bribery scandal, in which US authorities alleged that Siemens paid at least $4.5 million in bribes to secure Nigerian telecommunications contracts during the Obasanjo administration, with about $2.8 million reportedly passing through a bank account owned by Douglas, noting that Siemens subsequently agreed to pay approximately $1.6 billion in penalties to US and German authorities over global bribery violations. Further citing the William Jefferson bribery case, the APC said US court records indicated that former Congressman William Jefferson disclosed paying Atiku $100,000 to influence a proposed business partnership involving iGate and Netlink Digital Television, adding that Jefferson was eventually convicted and sentenced to prison. The party also referenced a 2010 report by the US Senate Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations, which it said linked Atiku and Douglas to more than $40 million in suspicious funds transferred into the United States through offshore companies and lodged in over 30 bank accounts associated with Douglas and her family. APC further faulted Atiku’s shift from his 2023 position favouring fuel subsidy removal to his new promise to restore the subsidy regime if elected, describing it as “his latest device to lay his hands on, and squander, the country’s 18-year foreign reserve high of over $54 billion built up from $3 billion by President Bola Tinubu in less than four years through bold and prudent economic reforms.” The ruling party said the treasury President Bola Tinubu had built strong was what Atiku desired “to scatter and plunder under the cover of his fake and unrealistic promise to restore the ruinous fuel subsidy regime.” The statement also cited former President Olusegun Obasanjo’s characterisation of Atiku in his book, My Watch, as possessing “a propensity for corruption, a tendency toward disloyalty, poor judgment, and a readiness to sacrifice the national interest for selfish gains.” It further recalled that in August 2026, Obasanjo described his decision to pick Atiku as his running mate in 1999 as the biggest mistake of his presidency, quoting him as saying, “The man I picked as my running mate, my number two, if I had known him as I came to know him later, I would not have picked him.” The post ‘Never again’, APC cautions Nigerians against voting Atiku in 2027 appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Nigeria’s Energy Transition must reflect development needs — Ekpo
items.description: By Obas Esiedesa, Abuja ABUJA — The Minister of State for Petroleum Resources (Gas), Rt. Hon. Ekperikpe Ekpo, has said Nigeria’s energy transition must reflect the country’s development realities, stressing that natural gas remains critical to meeting its immediate energy and industrial needs. Ekpo spoke on Thursday in Abuja at the 2026 Annual Conference of the Association of Energy Correspondents, Abuja (AECAF), with the theme, “Sustaining Oil and Gas Investment in Nigeria Amid Energy Transition.” He said while Nigeria supported the global drive towards cleaner and more sustainable energy systems, its transition must also address energy security, economic growth and industrialisation. According to him, millions of Nigerians still need reliable electricity and access to cleaner cooking fuels, while industries require affordable and dependable energy. “Natural gas therefore has an important role to play as a transition fuel and as an enabler of industrialisation,” he said. Ekpo said Nigeria remained endowed with significant oil and gas resources, adding that the government’s responsibility was to create an investment environment that would enable the resources to support industrialisation, job creation, infrastructure development and improved living standards. He identified policy stability, regulatory certainty, fiscal competitiveness, security and efficient project delivery as critical to sustaining investment in the petroleum sector. The minister said the implementation of the Petroleum Industry Act (PIA) 2021 and ongoing reforms were designed to provide greater clarity for investors, strengthen regulatory institutions and create a more competitive operating environment. He, however, acknowledged that legislation alone was insufficient to attract and retain investment, stressing that investors also needed confidence that government policies would be consistently implemented and projects executed efficiently and profitably. On gas development, Ekpo said the Federal Government was working to make Nigeria’s gas resources a stronger foundation for economic transformation through the Decade of Gas Initiative. He said the government was seeking to transform the role of gas from being primarily an export commodity to a resource increasingly supporting power generation, manufacturing, fertiliser production, petrochemicals, transportation and other productive activities. The minister also urged energy correspondents to provide accurate context and balanced analysis of developments in the sector, describing the media as an important stakeholder in building confidence in Nigeria’s investment environment. “Energy correspondents therefore have a critical responsibility not only to report developments, but also to provide the Nigerian public with accurate context and balanced analysis,” he said. Speaking at the conference, the Commission Chief Executive of the Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission (NUPRC), Engr. Oritsemeyiwa Eyesan, said Nigeria averaged about 1.68 million barrels per day of crude oil and condensate in August 2026, with crude production meeting the country’s OPEC quota for the fourth consecutive month. Eyesan, who was represented by NUPRC Director, Surface Development, Joseph Ogunsola, said the improvement provided a stronger base for pursuing production targets of two million barrels per day in the near term and three million barrels per day by 2030. She said the scale of investment opportunities in the upstream sector was already evident, noting that the commission had, since 2024, approved Field Development Plans representing more than $57 billion in investment. She added that 22 major offshore projects expected between 2026 and 2030 carried estimated investment potential of between $30 billion and $50 billion. Eyesan stressed that the priority was now to translate approvals and investment commitments into actual project execution and new production. Earlier, the Chairman of AECAF, Mr John Ofikhenua, said the conference was designed to stimulate discussion on how Nigeria could sustain investment in its hydrocarbon resources amid changing global energy priorities. Ofikhenua said investment in the oil and gas industry had been affected by adverse policies and global developments, citing the shale revolution in the United States, the COVID-19 pandemic and the growing global push for energy transition as factors that had contributed to investment contractions. He said Nigeria needed to sustain adherence to the Petroleum Industry Act, strengthen national security and maintain stable policies to preserve investor confidence and attract fresh capital into the petroleum industry. He particularly stressed the need to secure the Niger Delta, describing peace and stability in the region as important to sustaining oil and gas investment. items.title: Conseil des Ministres du 24 septembre 2026 : Le Gouvernement officialise les statuts de 315 Martyrs et 10 Invalides de la Nation et met fin au « laisser-faire » pour les associations et ONG
items.description: Le Conseil des Ministres s’est tenu, ce jeudi 24 septembre 2026, sous la présidence du Camarade Capitaine Ibrahim TRAORÉ, Président du Faso, Chef de l’État. Selon le Ministre Porte-parole du Gouvernement, Pingdwendé Gilbert OUÉDRAOGO, plusieurs dossiers ont été examinés et d'importantes décisions prises pour le plein épanouissement des Burkinabè dans la dynamique de la Révolution Progressiste Populaire (RPP). Au titre de la Primature et en application de la loi du 10 juin 2022 portant statut de martyr et d'invalide de la Nation, le Conseil a adopté deux décrets rendant hommage aux citoyens qui se sont illustrés par leur bravoure et leur sacrifice lors des récents événements politiques, sociaux et sécuritaires du pays, selon le Porte-parole du Gouvernement. En application de cette loi, « ces deux décrets visent la reconnaissance de la qualité de martyr de la Nation à 315 personnes et d'invalide de la Nation à 10 personnes », précise Camarade Pingdwendé Gilbert OUÉDRAOGO, Porte-parole du Gouvernement. Les personnes reconnues invalides de la Nation bénéficient, entre autres, de la gratuité du transport et des soins publics, la prise en charge psychosociale et la prise en charge de leurs enfants mineurs en qualité de pupilles de la Nation. Les personnes reconnues martyrs de la Nation bénéficient de la prise en charge de leurs enfants mineurs en qualité de pupilles de la Nation, d’une prise en charge psychosociale des ayants droit ainsi que des frais de transport et d'inhumation. « Ces mesures visent à apporter un soutien concret et pérenne aux familles et aux ayants droits confrontés à des situations de vulnérabilité, concrétisant ainsi la gratitude solennelle de la Nation burkinabè envers ses héros », souligne le Ministre OUÉDRAOGO. Création de « FASO SANYA » pour l’entretien des édifices publiques Pour le compte du ministère l’Économie et des Finances, le Conseil a adopté plusieurs décrets s'inscrivant dans la dynamique du Plan R.E.L.A.N.C.E. Face au constat d'un mauvais entretien généralisé des bâtiments publics dû aux lourdeurs administratives, l'État a décidé de la création de FASO SANYA, une structure dédiée à la maintenance (nettoyage, plomberie, électricité, climatisation, rénovation). Ce nouvel Établissement public à caractère administratif (EPA) travaillera en collaboration avec la Maison des Compétences Burkina Suudu Bawdè pour mobiliser des coopératives d'ouvriers qualifiés pour des interventions agiles et ciblées. En vue de veiller au respect des priorités nationales et garantir l'impact réel des financements, le Conseil a adopté deux décrets fixant les conditions d'obtention du statut d'ONG. Selon le Ministre Aboubakar NAKANABO, des textes d'application formalisent désormais l'attribution du statut officiel d'ONG : « un accord-cadre sera obligatoire pour les associations de droit burkinabè et une convention de siège régira les entités étrangères ». Un délai de grâce de deux ans est accordé aux organisations pour se conformer aux nouvelles exigences. 80 % des ressources mobilisées doivent aller directement au terrain Désormais, toute ONG intervenant au Burkina Faso devra consacrer au moins 80 % de son budget global aux investissements directs. Pour le Gouvernement, il s’agit d’éviter que les fonds levés au nom des populations vulnérables ne soient absorbés par des frais de fonctionnement, et de garantir un impact réel sur le quotidien des citoyens. Au titre du Ministère de la Santé, le Conseil a adopté le projet de loi portant Code de la santé publique. Rendue indispensable par l'obsolescence du texte précédent datant de 1994, cette réforme majeure vise à doter les professionnels d'un outil de régulation moderne pour améliorer la prise en charge médicale et garantir un accès équitable aux soins à l'ensemble de la population, selon le Camarade Ministre de la Santé, Robert Lucien Jean Claude KARGOUGOU. Au nombre des innovations, on note l’intégration de textes sur le don d'organes et la promotion du secteur privé de santé, la prise en compte explicite des soins palliatifs à tous les niveaux de la pyramide sanitaire, le renforcement de la vigilance sanitaire et de la régulation du marché pharmaceutique, la création d'un corps de réserve sanitaire et la réglementation renforcée de la médecine légale et de la chirurgie plastique. items.title: New York : « En voulant salir le Président, l’opposition s’est tirée une balle dans le pied » (Alhoussein Makanéra Kaké)
items.description: C’est par cette formule que l’honorable Alhoussein Makanéra Kaké, président du groupe parlementaire GMD, résume sa lecture des manifestations organisées à New York contre le président Mamadi Doumbouya. Dans une déclaration, le parlementaire affirme que la contestation politique demeure un droit reconnu, tout en estimant que certaines formes d’expression ont dépassé les limites du débat démocratique. « Nous n’avons jamais dit que nous avions élu un monarque. Nous n’avons pas élu un roi, encore moins un dieu. Le Général Mamadi Doumbouya est un Président de la République, et à ce titre, il n’est ni au-dessus de la critique ni à l’abri de la contradiction », déclare-t-il. Pour lui, la démocratie implique l’existence de différentes opinions, y compris celles qui sont opposées au pouvoir en place. « Manifester contre le Président est un droit démocratique. Manifester en sa faveur en est également un. Nous félicitons tous ceux qui ont manifesté dans l’ordre, la discipline et le respect des lois, qu’ils soient pour ou contre le Président », poursuit l’honorable Alhoussein Makanéra Kaké. Toutefois, il dit condamner les comportements qu’il attribue à certains manifestants. « La démocratie se nourrit de la contradiction, pas de la violence », soutient-il. Revenant sur les événements de New York, le président du groupe parlementaire de la mouvance présidentielle estime que ceux qui voulaient porter atteinte à l’image du chef de l’État auraient, selon lui, obtenu un résultat inverse. « Mais ceux qui ont choisi les insultes, la haine, les intimidations et la violence contre leur Président et contre leur propre pays ont commis une grave erreur politique. En voulant salir l’image du Général Mamadi Doumbouya, ils ont exposé au monde leur propre visage », affirme-t-il. Avant d’ajouter : « En voulant affaiblir le Président, ils ont renforcé la position de son gouvernement ! » Dans sa déclaration, l’honorable Alhoussein Makanéra Kaké rappelle également les positions défendues par la mouvance présidentielle sur la nécessité de préserver la paix et la cohésion nationale. « Nous avons toujours affirmé que le gouvernement guinéen est engagé en faveur de la paix, de la quiétude sociale, de la tranquillité et de la cohésion nationale. Nous avons également dénoncé les discours de haine et les dérives violentes de certains acteurs de l’opposition », indique-t-il. Selon lui, les critiques dont il dit avoir fait l’objet n’ont pas empêché les événements récents de confirmer, à ses yeux, les alertes lancées par la majorité présidentielle. « Nous avons été critiqués, incompris et parfois accusés d’exagération. Aujourd’hui, les événements de New York viennent malheureusement illustrer nos mises en garde », poursuit-il. Le parlementaire évoque également le contexte international, notamment l’Examen périodique universel (EPU) de la Guinée, prévu à Genève, en Suisse. « Le plus ironique, c’est qu’à l’approche de l’Examen périodique universel (EPU) de la Guinée, à Genève, en Suisse, ceux qui voulaient accabler le gouvernement guinéen viennent de lui fournir, à New York, des arguments qu’il n’aurait même pas eu besoin de chercher », estime-t-il. Poursuivant son analyse, il affirme que les actions de l’opposition auraient finalement servi la communication du gouvernement. « En voulant être les accusateurs du Président Mamadi Doumbouya, ils se sont transformés en ses propres avocats contre eux-mêmes ! Ils ont voulu charger le dossier du gouvernement, mais ils ont fini par plaider en sa faveur, en illustrant précisément ce que celui-ci dénonce depuis toujours : la haine, l’intolérance et la violence politique », déclare-t-il. Pour l’honorable Alhoussein Makanéra Kaké, le débat politique doit rester fondé sur les idées et non sur les attaques personnelles. « La démocratie, ce n’est pas aimer obligatoirement le Président. C’est accepter que d’autres l’aiment, le soutiennent ou le contestent sans que la haine et la violence ne deviennent des moyens d’expression », rappelle-t-il. Il appelle enfin les différents acteurs politiques à préserver l’image du pays. « La Guinée appartient à tous les Guinéens, majorité comme opposition. Aucun désaccord politique ne justifie de salir son pays, d’insulter ses compatriotes ou de recourir à la violence », conclut-il. Dans sa dernière partie, le président du groupe parlementaire de la mouvance présidentielle réaffirme son analyse selon laquelle les manifestations de New York auraient eu un effet contraire à celui recherché. « En voulant combattre le Général Mamadi Doumbouya, certains ont surtout contribué à conforter le discours de son gouvernement : la paix et la stabilité d’un côté, la haine et la violence de l’autre. Quelle erreur politique ! À force de vouloir tirer sur le Président, ils ont fini par se tirer une balle dans le pied », conclut l’honorable Alhoussein Makanéra Kaké. Christine Finda Kamano L’article New York : « En voulant salir le Président, l’opposition s’est tirée une balle dans le pied » (Alhoussein Makanéra Kaké) est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.description: ​Les prévisions de l'Institut national de la météorologie annoncent la poursuite de pluies temporairement orageuses, cette nuit, dans plusieurs régions du pays. Ces pluies sont attendues en particulier dans le sud tunisien, pouvant être localement abondantes à l'extrême sud, précise la même source en ajoutant que des passages nuageux sont prévus pour le reste du pays. items.title: Ecobank Group commits US$2.6bn to women-led businesses and agribusinesses across Africa
items.description: Ecobank Group has announced a combined USD 2.6 billion lending commitment by 2030 to support women-owned businesses and agricultural value chains across its 34 African markets. The announcement was made during the Ecobank@40 Media Conference in Lomé, as the pan-African banking group marked the conclusion of its 40th anniversary year. The commitments comprise USD 2.0 billion for women entrepreneurs through the bank’s flagship Ellevate programme and USD 600 million for agriculture-focused small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). Ecobank says the initiatives form part of its next phase of growth, with a focus on economic transformation, financial inclusion and sustainable development across Africa. USD 2.0 billion for women-led enterprises Under its Ellevate by Ecobank programme, the Group plans to build an outstanding loan portfolio of USD 2.0 billion dedicated to women entrepreneurs by 2030. The initiative builds on support already provided to more than 110,000 women-led enterprises, with the bank targeting an increase in its registered client base to 400,000 formal businesses. Ecobank also plans to expand digital onboarding and financial inclusion initiatives, with the strategy expected to create funding pathways for up to 1 million female micro-entrepreneurs across the continent. The expanded Ellevate framework will provide unsecured and partially secured credit facilities, supported by strategic development finance institution guarantee partnerships. The programme will focus particularly on sectors including agribusiness, education and healthcare. USD 600 million for agribusiness SMEs Ecobank has also committed USD 600 million in outstanding loans dedicated exclusively to Agric-focused SMEs by 2030. The initiative is designed to support the wider agricultural value chain rather than focusing solely on seasonal harvest financing. Under the “Farm-to-Fork” approach, financing will target farmers, aggregators, processors, logistics providers, traders and exporters. The strategy will also prioritise climate-smart agriculture, digital payment channels across rural supply chains and structured trade finance. Ecobank says the approach is intended to support regional food markets while reducing Africa’s dependence on food imports. Expanding access to African markets A key component of both commitments is the Ecobank Single Market Trade Hub, a digital marketplace connecting more than 60,000 businesses across Africa. Through the Trade Hub and Ecobank’s pan-African payment infrastructure, women entrepreneurs in agriculture and commercial SMEs will have access to cross-border buyers and suppliers, alongside multi-currency payment services under the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA). Ecobank says it will pursue the initiatives through four strategic areas: expanded credit and de-risking, cross-border trade and AfCFTA acceleration, digitalisation of value chains, and capacity building and ESG integration. The financing will include working capital, trade loans, and investment financing supported by guarantees from development finance institutions and risk-sharing facilities. The bank also plans to provide business management, export readiness, leadership and sustainable agricultural training. Commenting on the commitments, CEO of Ecobank Group, Jeremy Awori, said the bank’s 40th anniversary would serve as a foundation for its next phase of growth. “We are using the conclusion of our 40th anniversary as a strategic launchpad for Africa’s next economic chapter,” said Jeremy Awori, CEO of Ecobank Group. “Africa cannot industrialise by financing harvests alone, nor can it achieve its full potential while women face structural capital gaps. By committing USD 2.0 billion to women entrepreneurs and USD 600 million to agricultural value chains, we are turning gender-smart financing and food sovereignty into the primary engines of African growth,” he added. The commitments build on Ecobank’s founding vision, established 40 years ago in Lomé, which aimed to create an African bank built by Africans and focused on supporting the continent’s economic development and financial integration.

items.title: CAN 2027 (Q) : Tout savoir sur le Mozambique, futur adversaire du Sénégal
items.description: Le Sénégal, champion d’Afrique en titre, débute sa campagne de qualification pour la CAN 2027 ce vendredi 25 septembre 2026 avec un déplacement au Mozambique. Les Mambas, habitués des joutes africaines, ne viendront pas en victimes expiatoires, loin de là. Voici tout ce qu’il faut savoir sur cette équipe menée par le stratège Chiquinho Condé. Le pays Capitale : Maputo Superficie : 801 590 km2 Population : 33 635 160 habitants Langue officielle : Portugais Habitants : Mozambicains / Mozambicaines Surnom de l'équipe : Os Mambas (Les Mambas) Le Mozambique et la CAN Titre(s) : 0 Finale(s) : 0 Participations : 6 Leur première apparition remonte à 1986. Ils se sont ensuite qualifiés pour les éditions 1996, 1998, 2010, 2023 et 2025. Pays hôte : 0 Parcours à la CAN 1986 : éliminé au 1er tour 1996 : éliminé au 1er tour 1998 : éliminé au 1er tour 2010 : éliminé au 1er tour 2023 : éliminé au 1er tour 2025 : 1/8e de finale Chiquinho Conde, l’architecte Depuis quelques années, le Mozambique est devenu un véritable poil à gratter pour ses adversaires. Les Mambas connaissent d’ailleurs une progression notable. En se qualifiant pour la CAN 2025, le pays a réussi à disputer une deuxième édition de Coupe d’Afrique pour la 2e fois seulement de son histoire après les éditions 1996 et 1998. Et pour couronner le tout, les Mozambicains ont atteint les 1/8e de finale au Maroc, sortant ainsi des poules pour la première fois de leur histoire. Cette progression est due en grande partie à un homme : Chiquinho Condé. Sélectionneur depuis 2021, il avait déjà permis au Mozambique d’accrocher l’Égypte et le Ghana (2-2) lors de la CAN 2023, avant de briller à la CAN 2025 avec notamment une belle victoire contre le Gabon en poules (3-2). Les Mambas, qui produisent un football de très belle qualité, sont souvent très dangereux en contre. Joueur à suivre : « Génie » Catamo En défense, le Mozambique pouvait compter sur un joueur à la fois costaud défensivement et très bon techniquement : Reinildo. Néanmoins, le footballeur passé notamment par Lille (3 saisons), l’Atlético Madrid (3 saisons) et actuellement à Sunderland, a décidé de mettre un terme à sa carrière internationale. En son absence, le véritable référent de cette équipe n’est autre que Geny Catamo. Les amateurs de Ligue des champions et du championnat portugais sont sans doute familiers avec ce nom puisqu’il évolue au Sporting Club Portugal depuis 2021 (avec deux prêts entre 2021 et 2023). Le gaucher de 25 ans, qui évolue comme milieu offensif droit ou derrière l’attaquant, est devenu une pièce maîtresse du club lisboète, totalisant déjà 2 buts et 3 passes décisives en 8 rencontres cette saison. Lors de l’exercice écoulé, il avait planté 7 pions et délivré 3 offrandes. Avec le Mozambique, Geny Catamo a franchi un cap historique en 2026, devenant le meilleur buteur de l’histoire des Mambas avec 15 réalisations. Ses forces : la percussion, le dribble, le positionnement entre les lignes, la capacité de sortir des passes venues d’ailleurs, et une frappe redoutable. À noter que l’équipe du Mozambique est en totale mutation puisque, par rapport à la dernière CAN, 9 joueurs sont sortis du groupe : Ivane Urrubal, gardien (UD Songo), Mexer, défenseur (Ankara Keçiörengücü, Turquie), Reinildo Mandava, défenseur (Sunderland, retraite internationale), Ifren Matola, défenseur (UD Songo), Nené, défenseur (Abu Salim, Liban), Domingues, milieu (UD Songo), Kenys Abdala, milieu (GD Chaves B, Portugal), João Bonde, milieu (Ferroviário da Beira), Melque, attaquant (UD Songo) ; tandis que neuf joueurs effectuent leur entrée : Guirrugo (gardien), Bruno Wilson, Valter Nhacussa, Celton Jamisse et Feliciano Jone (défenseurs), Cândido Mathe et Edson Macuacua (milieux), Alcides Raice et Dayo António (attaquants). Une équipe qui réussit au Sénégal Le Sénégal a déjà affronté le Mozambique trois fois en match officiel, et les Lions ont remporté le duel à chaque fois. Il y a d’abord eu une confrontation lors de la CAN 1986 où le Sénégal avait gagné 2-0 en poules. Puis, lors des qualifications pour la CAN 2023, Sadio Mané et ses coéquipiers avaient glané un succès à l’aller (5-1) et au retour (1-0). Oumar Boubacar NDONGO

items.title: ‘I feel immense emotion’ — Zidane ahead of first France match
items.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Zinedine Zidane has admitted the significance of taking charge of France for the first time as he prepares to begin his reign against Turkey in the Nations League on Friday. The 54-year-old succeeded Didier Deschamps following the former France captain’s 14-year spell in charge and will officially begin his tenure with an away fixture in Kocaeli. Speaking at his pre-match press conference, Zidane was asked whether his emotions were comparable to those he experienced when he made his France debut 32 years ago. “Maybe even more, actually,” Zidane said. “It was a long time ago, and today I feel an immense emotion at being here in charge of this France team.” Zidane’s appointment has generated huge interest in France, with his first week in charge dominating media coverage ahead of his first competitive match. The former Real Madrid manager, however, insisted the focus should remain on his players rather than his own status. “It’s the next step after Didier’s 14 years, it’s something new so it’s completely normal. But the main protagonists are the players,” he said. “I think you just have to accept the way things are done; I’m not looking for that and I’m not here for that. “I’m going to try to do the job with my players, to make sure we can win matches – that’s what interests me.” France midfielder Adrien Rabiot said Zidane has also tried to minimise the attention surrounding his appointment and allow the players to express themselves. “He is with us the way he is on the outside,” Rabiot said. “We’re fully aware of how important he’s been for French football. His aura means he takes up a lot of space and people expect a lot from him.” Rabiot, who is one of France’s captains alongside Kylian Mbappe, Ousmane Dembele and Jules Kounde, said several changes have already been noticeable since Zidane replaced Deschamps. “Some players already, different ways of doing things and also different training sessions,” he said. “What the coach wants is obviously a fairly attacking style of play. “We’ll be very closely watched for how we play because the coach is new and a lot is expected from him.” Zidane will have to wait until next Friday to lead France in a home match, with his first two fixtures coming away from home. France face Turkey on Friday before travelling to play Belgium on Monday, while Zidane’s first home game will come against Italy next Friday. items.title: DEEP SEA PORT: Tinubu assures investors of regulatory clarity as Ogun, DP World sign $7bn MoUs
items.description: PARIS — President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has assured investors of regulatory clarity, policy stability and a predictable business environment as the Ogun State Government and DP World signed memoranda of understanding, MoUs, for the development of major port and industrial projects estimated at over $7 billion. The MoUs, signed in Paris on Thursday, cover the Ogun State Blue Marine Special Economic Zone and the Gateway Deep Seaport. Tinubu, who witnessed the signing ceremony, said the Federal Government would continue to create the conditions necessary for investors to commit long-term capital to Nigeria. According to the President, the government is committed to providing regulatory certainty and removing bottlenecks that could hinder the implementation of major investments. The Ogun State delegation was led by Governor Dapo Abiodun, while representatives of DP World and other stakeholders also attended the ceremony. The proposed Gateway Deep Seaport is expected to feature a four-kilometre berth and an 18-metre draft, with the capacity to handle large vessels and support increased maritime and commercial activities. The project is also expected to provide an alternative gateway for cargoes currently passing through Lagos ports, potentially reducing pressure on the Apapa and Tin Can Island port corridors. The Blue Marine Special Economic Zone, covering about 10,000 hectares, is designed to attract manufacturing, logistics and other industrial investments and promote value addition. The projects are projected to generate more than 50,000 direct jobs, alongside additional indirect employment opportunities. Tinubu said the investments aligned with the Federal Government’s efforts to diversify the economy, strengthen infrastructure and position Nigeria as a major destination for international capital. He said the Federal Government would facilitate the provision of supporting infrastructure, including road, rail and power connections, while also strengthening maritime security and reducing bureaucratic bottlenecks. The President also highlighted the importance of linking the projects with existing and planned transport infrastructure, including the Ogun section of the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway. The proposed developments are expected to complement other planned infrastructure in the area, including maritime and energy facilities. Governor Abiodun said the projects would deepen Ogun’s industrialisation drive and strengthen the state’s position as a major investment destination. The Ogun Government said the Blue Marine Special Economic Zone would provide an integrated platform for manufacturers and other businesses seeking to establish operations close to major transportation and maritime infrastructure. The proposed Gateway Deep Seaport is also expected to expand Nigeria’s maritime capacity, improve logistics and support the movement of goods into and out of the country. The agreements form part of efforts by the Ogun State Government and its international partners to attract large-scale private investment into infrastructure, manufacturing and logistics. The Federal Government is expected to work with the state government and investors to facilitate the necessary approvals and infrastructure required for the implementation of the projects. items.title: Daara Aïcha Oummoul Mouminine : à une semaine de ses 30 ans, l’école sollicite l’appui de l’État
items.description: Reçue en audience par le Premier ministre Ahmadou Al Aminou Lô ce 24 septembre 2026, une délégation du Daara Aïcha Oummoul Mouminine a exposé ses difficultés de fonctionnement et demandé un soutien pour la réussite de la célébration de son trentenaire. Le Premier ministre Ahmadou Al Aminou Lo a reçu ce jeudi une délégation du Daara Aïcha Oummoul Mouminine, conduite par Mme Adja Bineta Thiaw. Les échanges ont porté sur le 30e anniversaire de l'institution, prévu le samedi 3 octobre 2026, ainsi que sur « la gestion quotidienne de l'école et les difficultés de fonctionnement auxquelles elle est confrontée », selon le communiqué du gouvernement. La délégation a sollicité l'appui du chef du gouvernement pour la réussite de la cérémonie. Elle a aussi exposé les difficultés structurelles de l'établissement, liées notamment « au recrutement d'enseignants, à la prise en charge de denrées alimentaires, aux équipements administratifs et pédagogiques ». Le Premier ministre « a promis de faire saisir le ministre de l'Intérieur, le ministre chargé de la Famille et les autres services concernés, afin qu'ils apportent leur soutien ». Le communiqué ne précise ni la nature ni le calendrier de cet appui. Créé en octobre 1996, le Daara se consacre à « la formation intégrale des jeunes filles en associant la mémorisation du Saint Coran, les sciences islamiques et l'enseignement général ». Il compte aujourd'hui 2 565 élèves, dont 1 336 pensionnaires internes, soit un peu plus de la moitié de l'effectif. Il emploie 239 personnes, dont 152 enseignants. O.B.N

items.title: Ouagadougou: 4 présumés spécialistes de vols à main armée et blanchiment de capitaux aux arrêts
items.description: Dans le cadre de la lutte contre la criminalité urbaine, la Police Nationale du Burkina Faso, à travers son Commissariat de l’Arrondissement n°9 de Ouagadougou, a démantelé un réseau de malfrats présumés spécialistes de vols à main armée, le blanchiment de capitaux et la consommation de stupéfiants, selon un communiqué de l’institution policière, ce jeudi 24 septembre 2026. « Le Commissariat de Police de l’Arrondissement (CPA) n°09 de la ville de Ouagadougou a mis fin aux activités illicites d’un réseau de malfrats qui s’étaient spécialisés entre autres dans les vols à main armée, le blanchiment de capitaux et la consommation de stupéfiants dans la capitale burkinabè. Relativement au mode opératoire du groupe, ses membres, dont l’âge est compris entre 28 et 44 ans et parmi lesquels des repris de justice, sillonnaient nuitamment en binômes plusieurs quartiers de la ville, notamment Yagma, Bassinko, Bissighin, Marcoussis, Kilwin, Tampouy et Kamboinsin à la recherche de potentielles victimes. Dès qu’ils en identifiaient une, ils la filaient jusqu’à ce qu’elle se retrouve isolée dans les zones peu ou mal éclairées, dans les six mètres ou à l’entrée des domiciles. A l’aide de leur arme à feu, ils faisaient irruption, tenaient en respect la victime et la dépouillaient de son engin et de tout objet trouvé en sa possession. Pour éviter de se faire identifier, ils se masquaient soigneusement avant de passer à l’acte. Les biens volés étaient revendus sur place ou convoyés dans les pays voisins pour y être écoulés. Une partie du gain était partagée entre les membres du groupe et l’autre partie était réinvestie dans l’achat de terrains et d’autres biens. Grâce à la collaboration des populations, les enquêteurs ont, au moment de l’interpellation des malfrats, saisi plusieurs objets dont un pistolet automatique, des munitions, un véhicule et des motos. La Police Nationale remercie encore une fois les citoyens grâce à qui ce résultat a été atteint. Elle les invite à plus de vigilance et de prudence autour d’eux, particulièrement à limiter les déplacements tardifs, à éviter les lieux peu ou mal éclairés, à éclairer l’entrée de leurs domiciles et à poursuivre la dénonciation des cas suspects aux numéros verts que sont les 17, 16 et 1010. » La Police Nationale, une force publique au service des citoyens ! items.title: Full list: Atiku appoints Ibrahim-Imam, El-Rufai, Dino Melaye, others to ADC Campaign Council
items.description: ABUJA — Presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress, ADC, Atiku Abubakar, has approved the composition of his Presidential Campaign Council ahead of the 2027 general elections, naming Kashim Ibrahim-Imam as chairman and former Kaduna State Governor, Nasir El-Rufai, as deputy chairman. Read Also: Petrol Price Surge: FG gains, workers suffer — NLC; N70,000 wage inadequate – Keyamo The appointments were announced Thursday by Phrank Shaibu, Director of Strategic Communication of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council and Senior Special Assistant on Public Communication to Atiku. Senator Austin Akobundu was named Director-General and Campaign Manager, with responsibility for coordinating the campaign’s operations and translating its strategy into action. According to Shaibu, the campaign structure comprises six Deputy Directors-General overseeing operational directorates, with 30 directors assigned specific responsibilities. Veteran journalist and publisher, Dele Momodu, will head the Media and Communications Directorate, while former Kogi West Senator, Dino Melaye, will lead Contact and Mobilisation. The Policy Team will be chaired by economist and banker Mohammed Hayatudeen, who will work with Professor Mohammed Sagagi and other members, including Professor Kingsley Moghalu. Former Edo State Governor and pioneer National Chairman of the All Progressives Congress, APC, John Oyegun, will chair the Campaign Advisory Board. Shaibu said the structure was deliberately designed as a lean, people-driven organisation in response to the economic challenges facing Nigerians. He said the campaign would focus on issues including the cost of living, unemployment, insecurity and declining purchasing power. “When families are struggling with food prices, transport costs and shrinking incomes, a campaign asking for their trust must show discipline in how it operates,” Shaibu said. He added that the structure was designed to give each directorate a clearly defined responsibility and ensure that appointees were accountable for results. “Our measure of success will be how clearly we address the cost of living, unemployment, insecurity and declining purchasing power—and how effectively we organise to make Nigeria affordable again,” he said. The campaign council is expected to coordinate Atiku’s presidential campaign activities nationwide ahead of the 2027 election. The ADC had earlier submitted Atiku’s name as its presidential candidate and former Rivers State governor, Rotimi Amaechi, as vice-presidential candidate to the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC. items.title: After seizing Tigray airports, TPLF announces ‘defensive war’ against Ethiopian govt
items.description: The confrontation between the Tigray regional government and the Ethiopian federal government entered a new phase on Wednesday when Tigrayan forces seized control of the Mekelle, Axum and Shire airports. Clashes broke out at several locations in the restive northern state, the site of a two-year civil war that concluded in 2022, and in the neighboring Afar region — a development that has pushed the Ethiopian conflict back toward open warfare, four years after the signing of the Pretoria Agreement that ended the previous war between the Tigray People’s Liberation Front and federal forces. A source in the Tigray regional administration told Mada Masr that the seizure of the airports was part of a military redeployment that began in the early hours of Wednesday, with Tigrayan forces using the airports as facilities of operational importance amid the expanding scope of the fighting. In the wake of the TPLF takeover, Ethiopian Airlines announced the suspension of flights to the three airports due to the “current situation” in the Tigray region. A Tigrayan military source noted that Wednesday’s developments followed months of troop buildup and limited skirmishes along the front lines, describing Wednesday’s events as a shift from a phase of mutual pressure to direct confrontation. He added that Tigrayan forces view federal movements as an attempt to alter the military landscape established since the Pretoria Agreement and believe that seizing certain vital sites could prevent federal forces from utilizing the region’s civilian and military infrastructure during ongoing operations. The federal government framed Wednesday’s events differently. A former security source in Addis Ababa described the movements by the TPLF as a “full-scale attack” on government positions in Afar and Amhara. While seizing airports does not in itself decide the outcome of the battle, it signals a shift in the nature of operations, a security source in Addis Ababa told Mada Masr. Mekelle serves as the region’s political and administrative hub, while the airports at Axum and Shire provide crucial links to northern and western Tigray. Consequently, placing airports under the control of regional forces strains the federal government’s ability to manage its presence within the region and gives Tigrayan forces a strategic advantage in any future negotiations, the source said. The security source added that any operation to retake the airports would require careful calculation due to the presence of civilians in the cities, and because the use of air power and artillery in urban areas would heighten humanitarian risks. In its first official comment on Wednesday’s escalation, the Ethiopian military said it had repelled attacks from Tigrayan forces and their allies in parts of northern Ethiopia, adding that hostilities began in an area of the Amhara region close to the border with Tigray. The military added that it had killed 272 Tigrayan fighters and wounded 260 in a counteroffensive in the Amhara region. Wednesday’s escalation in the long simmering tension between the TPLF and federal government immediately follows a series of airstrikes that targeted areas in Tigray over the past few days. In Alamata, located in southern Tigray, an attack on Tuesday left 14 civilians dead and 22 injured, a local media source told Mada Masr. Aftermath of a drone strike on a humanitarian aid truck in northwestern Tigray, September 22. Photo: @JoeTseGy on X. The source stated that more than six drones and three fighter jets carried out over 21 raids, beginning around 3:30 am, adding that the strikes hit civilian educational facilities, including a secondary school. The media source noted that the area has recently seen an increase in military activity and troop movements involving both federal and Tigrayan forces. The TPLF is increasingly worried about drone strikes, a senior official in the front told Mada Masr, saying that many top officials are limiting their movements to avoid being targeted by federal forces. For the security source in Addis Ababa, the broader concern for the federal government is that the conflict will quickly extend beyond Tigray. Wednesday’s clashes broke out just as the TPLF — alongside six other armed groups — announced the formation of the Ethiopian Peoples’ Forces Alliance for Survival. This alliance includes the Fano militia in Amhara, the Oromo Liberation Army, and groups from Afar, Benishangul-Gumuz and the Ogaden region. On Sunday, the seven groups declared their objective: to topple Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed’s government and establish a transitional administration. The security source states that the official announcement of the new opposition front alters federal calculations, as any prolonged confrontation in Tigray would necessitate the distribution of forces across multiple theaters of operation. The source added that the government is already contending with the Fano insurgency in Amhara and the OLA in Oromia. An expansion of the war in the north could overwhelm the federal army’s capacity to manage these fronts simultaneously. The source adds that an expansion of the fighting would directly impact regional dynamics, given these areas’ proximity to Ethiopia’s borders with Eritrea and Sudan. From the Tigrayan perspective, the Tigrayan military source views the new alliance as a shift in the war’s political landscape. The source noted that, unlike in its previous conflict with the federal government, the TPLF is entering the current confrontation as part of a broader network of Ethiopian armed groups. A source familiar with the Tigray regional administration states that the decision to engage in a “defensive war” followed what the regional leadership views as a series of federal measures that reshaped the security landscape surrounding the region. In recent months, the TPLF has accused the government of failing to implement key provisions of the Pretoria Agreement — specifically those concerning disputed territories, the return of displaced persons and the restructuring of civil administration in contested areas. The source adds that, for the leadership in Mekelle , Wednesday’s events represent a de facto collapse of the security arrangements established following the Pretoria Agreement. The seizure of the airports, the source noted, was part of an effort to consolidate control over the region and prevent federal forces from redeploying units within it. Tigray’s leadership believes that continued military pressure will reduce the agreement to a mere legal framework existing only on paper, while realities on the ground establish a new basis for the relationship between the two sides, the source said. The current escalation follows months of repeated warnings that the Pretoria Agreement could collapse. In August, federal forces clashed with a Tigrayan force known as the 70th Army near Shererina . This was followed by artillery and air strikes on Tigrayan positions. A former Ethiopian official stated that the federal operations aimed to “protect the constitutional order” and prevent the peace agreement from falling apart. On Wednesday, the United Nations warned of the rapidly deteriorating situation in northern Ethiopia, citing reports that the airports in Mekelle , Axum and Shire had been seized, and called on all parties to de-escalate, protect civilians and resume dialogue within the framework of the Pretoria Agreement. While the UN remained neutral, other major international players have singled out the TPLF as the culprit behind the escalation. United Kingdom Minister of State for Development and Africa Kirsty McNeill condemned on X the “attacks by the Tigray Defence Forces” and called for an immediate deescalation. The US also laid the blame at the TPLF’s feet. “I am disappointed to see the leadership of the TPLF, that the United States sanctioned earlier this year, make the poor decision to launch a large-scale offensive today,” US Ambassador to Ethiopia Ervin Massinga said in a statement released by the embassy in Addis Ababa. “Rejecting dialogue sponsored by the [African Union] under President [Olusegun] Obasanjo and engaging in an unwinnable fight does nothing for the people. Other armed groups would be wise to avoid this. While the US has tools to sanction additional leaders who try to push Ethiopia down the wrong path, I still believe a reasonable political dialogue is the right way to go.” The post After seizing Tigray airports, TPLF announces ‘defensive war’ against Ethiopian govt first appeared on Mada Masr .

items.title: Ghana to host high-level conference on scaling education initiatives in emergencies
items.description: Ghana will host West Africa’s second high-level conference on scaling education initiatives in emergencies, bringing together researchers, innovators, financiers, and academics from across the world to deliberate on how education systems can remain resilient during crises. The conference, scheduled for September 29 and 30, 2026, in Accra, will focus on practical strategies for protecting education during emergencies, scaling successful interventions beyond pilot stages and mobilising sustainable financing for education responses during and after crises. The Minister for Education, Haruna Iddrisu, in a press conference on Thursday, September 24, said the conference would seek answers to four critical questions: what works when a crisis forces schools to close; what it takes to scale successful interventions beyond pilot projects; who finances education interventions when ministries and their agencies lack emergency contingency funds; and what countries in the West African region can do collectively to protect education during emergencies. He cited the COVID-19 pandemic as a major example of the disruption emergencies can cause to education systems. Following the closure of schools in March 2020, millions of learners from kindergarten through to tertiary education were sent home, with many losing significant instructional time and some unable to return to school. According to him, Ghana responded by introducing innovative and largely digital mechanisms to sustain learning during the pandemic. He said the country was now seeking to introduce additional innovative digital education mechanisms, tools and equipment from kindergarten through the basic education level, building on interventions already undertaken at the secondary level. The Minister noted that conflicts and other emergencies could have severe consequences for education, including increased dropout rates, teenage pregnancies, learning losses and worsening literacy and numeracy outcomes. He cited conflicts in areas such as Bawku, as well as developments in Burkina Faso and Mali, as examples of how conflict can disrupt education, noting that teachers may be forced to leave communities and schools, while learners and their families may relocate to safer areas. Mr Iddrisu also raised concerns about emergencies occurring in communities without access to electricity, radio, smartphones or other digital learning facilities, stressing that education interventions must therefore take into account the realities of vulnerable and underserved communities. He further highlighted the impact of the Akosombo Dam spillage in October 2023, which submerged communities in parts of the North Tongu, Central Tongu and South Tongu areas of the Volta Region. Tens of thousands of people were displaced, while schools were either submerged or converted into shelters for displaced persons. He said the disaster resulted in the loss of school furniture, textbooks, records and examination preparations, disrupting teaching and learning at a time when affected learners were still expected to participate in national examinations. Other emergencies cited included tidal waves and coastal erosion affecting communities around Keta and other coastal areas, flooding in northern Ghana, the effects of the spillage of the Bagre Dam, seasonal floods in the Upper East, Northern, Savannah and Oti Regions, as well as communal and ethnic conflicts. He stressed that such emergencies also place considerable pressure on teachers and educational infrastructure. Despite these challenges, Mr Iddrisu said Ghana had not remained passive, pointing to interventions such as the expansion of Complementary and Accelerated Education for out-of-school children, particularly in northern Ghana, as well as investments in foundational learning. He said strengthening basic and foundational learning would be a major priority, warning that failure to get foundational education right could leave the country’s broader education system fragile. Again, he highlighted the contribution of development partners and organisations supporting foundational learning and accelerated education initiatives. On teacher development, he said efforts were also being made to strengthen teacher professionalism, including continuous professional education to improve teachers’ capacity to respond effectively to changing educational needs and challenges. The Minister called on innovators and implementers attending the conference to present not only successful models but also interventions that had failed, arguing that lessons from both successes and failures were important to improving education responses during emergencies. The Minister commended the Director of Associates for Change, Dr Leslie Casely-Hayford, for her continued evidence-based analysis of education policies and government budgets. He said her professional scrutiny had contributed to public understanding of education-sector challenges and encouraged her to continue drawing attention to areas requiring greater government attention, including special and inclusive education. He said the upcoming conference would provide an opportunity for Ghana and its international partners to move beyond discussions and develop practical approaches for ensuring that children continue to access quality education even when emergencies disrupt normal schooling.

items.title: US and Sudan trade statements over legitimacy and peace efforts
items.description: The United States and Sudan have traded statements over Washington’s rejection of both sides of Sudan’s war as legitimate constitutional authorities, with Khartoum insisting that any peace process must respect the country’s sovereignty and national institutions. In a 22 September statement , US State Department spokesman Thomas “Tommy” Pigott said neither the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) nor the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) had made serious commitments to an immediate truce, accusing both sides of having “redoubled combat operations and drone strikes which kill civilians”. Pigott said Washington was calling on the warring parties to accept a humanitarian truce without preconditions and enter an inclusive political dialogue leading to civilian government. He added that neither the SAF, the RSF nor their leaders “represent legitimate, constitutional governance for Sudan” and said the United States would seek to “raise the cost of continued conflict” for the warring parties and networks supporting them. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said at a press conference in New York on Wednesday that Sudan’s war would not be continuing without external support, saying “that war and that conflict and that crisis would not be happening were it not for the active participation of external actors” supporting the opposing sides. Rubio said progress would ultimately depend on those actors using their “influence and pressure” on their respective proxies to honour commitments they have made. Criticism of US moves Sudan analyst and former US National Security Council official Cameron Hudson described the US statement as a declaration of “a policy of regime change in Sudan”. In a post on X earlier this week , he said Washington had “painted itself into a corner” through sanctions, an arms embargo and visa restrictions, warning that its “maximum pressure” approach could leave little room for a negotiated exit. Sudan’s Foreign Ministry rejected the statement on Wednesday, saying any sustainable peace initiative must respect Sudan’s “sovereignty, unity, territorial integrity and legitimate national institutions”. The ministry said the government remained ready to engage with the US and other regional and international partners but rejected any political process that could legitimise what it described as a reality created by the RSF. It also accused external actors of contributing to the continuation of the war, saying serious peace efforts must address “external interventions and sources of illegal support”. The diplomatic tensions have also spilled into the Quartet , which brings together the United States, Saudi Arabia, Egypt and the United Arab Emirates. Saudi Arabia has reportedly threatened to withdraw from the mechanism over Washington’s refusal to grant SAF Commander and Sovereignty Council President Lt Gen Abdelfattah El Burhan a visa to attend the UN General Assembly, according to the Africa Report . Saudi officials have not publicly confirmed the reported threat. The visa dispute reportedly centres on US pressure for El Burhan to accept a proposed 90-day ceasefire. ONU : les patrons d’OpenAI et d’Anthropic appellent à encadrer l’IA sans tomber dans le catastrophisme
items.description: Devant le Conseil de sécurité de l’ONU, Sam Altman et Dario Amodei ont plaidé pour davantage de vigilance face aux risques liés à l’intelligence artificielle, tout en appelant à éviter aussi bien l’optimisme aveugle que le catastrophisme. Les dirigeants de plusieurs grandes entreprises de l’intelligence artificielle ont appelé mercredi à une vigilance accrue face au développement rapide de cette technologie, lors d’une réunion du Conseil de sécurité des Nations unies consacrée à ses risques et à sa gouvernance. Invité à s’exprimer aux côtés de Dario Amodei, patron d’Anthropic, et de Clément Delangue, dirigeant de Hugging Face, le patron d’OpenAI Sam Altman a estimé que l’évolution actuelle de l’IA « nécessite une attention extrême ». Il a notamment souligné les risques liés à l’automatisation croissante du développement des systèmes d’intelligence artificielle. Les dirigeants du secteur ont cherché à défendre une position intermédiaire. « Nous ne voulons pas tomber dans le piège de l’optimisme aveugle, mais nous ne pouvons pas céder non plus au catastrophisme », a déclaré Sam Altman, appelant à « trouver un juste milieu ». Cette prudence intervient après plusieurs incidents rapportés ces derniers mois autour de modèles d’IA avancés. Certains systèmes auraient notamment adopté des comportements inattendus lors de tests, notamment en s’écartant des objectifs fixés par leurs développeurs. Face à ces risques, plusieurs responsables du secteur appellent désormais à renforcer les mécanismes de sécurité et la coopération internationale. Anthropic promet de ralentir « autant que nécessaire » Dario Amodei est allé plus loin lors de son intervention devant le Conseil de sécurité. Le patron d’Anthropic a annoncé que son entreprise était prête à « ralentir autant que nécessaire » le développement de ses systèmes afin de s’assurer que chaque nouveau modèle commercialisé soit suffisamment sûr. Cette déclaration constitue un engagement unilatéral de la part d’Anthropic, alors que l’entreprise avait déjà appelé récemment à un ralentissement coordonné entre les principaux acteurs du secteur. Sam Altman a, de son côté, reconnu que l’industrie ne devait pas accepter des risques technologiques excessifs au seul motif que les bénéfices potentiels de l’IA seraient importants. Un débat international qui divise La question de la gouvernance mondiale de l’IA reste toutefois au cœur des divergences entre grandes puissances. Plusieurs pays souhaitent renforcer la coopération sous l’égide des Nations unies, voire créer un mécanisme international dédié à la supervision de l’intelligence artificielle. La Chine s’est notamment prononcée en faveur d’un rôle central de l’ONU dans cette gouvernance. Les États-Unis affichent une position différente. Leur représentant au Conseil de sécurité, Michael Kratsios, a reconnu que les capacités de l’IA progressaient rapidement, mais estimé que cela ne justifiait pas de mettre son développement « en pause » ni de le soumettre à des structures de gouvernance mondiale. La France défend, elle aussi, une coopération internationale renforcée. Le ministre français des Affaires étrangères Jean-Noël Barrot a appelé à travailler « dans le cadre des Nations unies » avec les entreprises afin de définir les règles de cette nouvelle étape technologique. Le débat se poursuit donc autour d’un équilibre difficile : permettre à l’IA de continuer à progresser tout en renforçant les garde-fous nécessaires pour limiter les risques liés à ses capacités croissantes. The post ONU : les patrons d’OpenAI et d’Anthropic appellent à encadrer l’IA sans tomber dans le catastrophisme appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Législatives 2026: Le RNI assume son recul électoral et reporte la question des alliances gouvernementales
items.description: « La position du parti aujourd'hui ne peut se résumer uniquement à un classement électoral », a déclaré jeudi, le dirigeant du Rassemblement national de indépendants (RNI), Mohamed Chouki, depuis le siège du parti à Rabat. Il a admis que les résultats du RNI sont en baisse par rapport au scrutin précédent et affirme ne pas vouloir minimiser ce recul ni chercher à le justifier. Chouki s'exprimait en conférence de presse, au lendemain de l'annonce des résultats provisoires des élections législatives du 23 septembre qui ont classé le Parti authenticité et modernité (PAM) en tête des suffrages avec 97 sièges. Saluant la victoire du PAM (arrivé en tête avec 97 sièges) au début de son mot, Mohamed Chouki a déclaré que le parti ne prenait pas position immédiatement sur la formation du prochain gouvernement. Il a indiqué que la question sera examinée par ses instances internes et que les décisions officielles seront communiquées ultérieurement. « La prochaine étape politique, le Rassemblement National des Indépendants ne devancera pas les décisions de ses instances » , a-t-il affirmé, en ajoutant que ces questions seront débattues au sein des organes compétents du parti, conformément aux procédures organisationnelles en vigueur et en harmonie avec l'intérêt national et les choix du parti. Le leader du RNI a annoncé également que le parti allait procéder à une évaluation objective et sereine de son bilan de cinq ans à la tête du gouvernement et de ses résultats. « Notre parti a abordé ces élections après cinq années passées à assumer la responsabilité de la conduite de l'action gouvernementale, au cours d'une période qui n'a pas été facile, marquée par des mutations et des défis successifs aux niveaux national et international » , a-t-il déclaré lors de son point de presse auquel Hespress FR a assisté. « Nous sommes entrés dans ce scrutin forts de notre bilan, de nos positions et de nos choix, que nous avons présentés aux Marocains tels qu'ils sont, avec ce qui a été accompli et ce qui reste comme chantiers nécessitant davantage de travail », a-t-il poursuivi. Sur le sujet des résultats du scrutin et alors que le RNI était arrivé en tête des suffrages en 2021, Mohamed Chouki, dont le parti est arrivé en seconde position selon les résultats provisoires, a indiqué qu'il ne faisait aucun doute que les résultats ont enregistré un « recul » par rapport au précédent scrutin, « et nous ne souhaitons ni minimiser la portée de ce recul ni lui chercher des justifications », a-t-il souligné. Chouki a ajouté qu'en politique, « de même que nous sommes fiers de la confiance des citoyens lorsque nos résultats progressent, nous devons également écouter attentivement leur message lorsqu'ils reculent » , en affirmant qu'il s'agit pour son parti, d'une règle fondamentale de la pratique démocratique et du respect de la volonté des électeurs. Malgré un recul, le chef du RNI a tenu a relativiser en expliquant qu'après ces cinq années passées à assumer la responsabilité gouvernementale, le parti de la colombe a « préservé un poids politique et électoral important, ainsi que sa place parmi les forces incontournables du paysage partisan national », en soulignant la conservation de la confiance d'une large frange de citoyennes et de citoyens. Pour Chouki, « la position du parti aujourd'hui ne peut se résumer uniquement à un classement électoral » , en affirmant que le Rassemblement National des Indépendants a accumulé une expérience politique, gouvernementale et organisationnelle importante, et d'un projet politique qu'il continuera de défendre et de développer. Le RNI a également maintenu qu’il était fier de son action gouvernementale et a annoncé un débat « serein et sérieux » sur les résultats pour en tirer les enseignements qu'il faut. « Nous écouterons davantage, nous réviserons ce qui mérite de l'être et nous corrigerons ce qui doit l'être » , a lancé le chef du RNI en estimant qu'un parti qui souhaite s'inscrire dans la durée « ne craint ni la critique ni les moments d'évaluation ». Et de conclure que les partis politiques forts ne se mesurent pas seulement à leur capacité à remporter des élections, mais aussi à leur aptitude à comprendre les mutations que connaît la société, à décrypter les messages des citoyens, qu'ils soient positifs ou critiques, et à renouveler leurs idées, leurs élites et leurs modes d'action.
